problems.scenario: 2. New patient with only an age (retry after a lost response)
problems.detail: Form → register_patient(uuid7, 'Sara', NULL, 'Haddad', 'female', '1971' [client: current year − 55], NULL, NULL, [], NULL). born_on_invalid passes (year form, not future), name_missing passes, record_number minted by the identity on insert, one patient_changes row {given_name: [null,'Sara'], …}. Then open_visit as in 1 → is_first true. The duplicate warning read_patients(org, 'Haddad', born_on '1971') narrows by year, so a year-only value still matches; age_on('1971', date) is ±1 year for field_range, acceptable. The strain is the retry key: the desk's first call commits but the response is lost; the client retries the same id with patient_change_id = NULL (it never loaded one) → a newer patient_changes row now exists → changed_since_read is raised on what is a retry and the form is stuck until it refetches. Spec 01 gives entries 'a retry with the same id returns the stored row and changes nothing'; spec 03 says only 'a second call edits'.
problems.fix: One rule sentence on register_patient, spec 01's retry rule verbatim: a call whose columns and identifiers equal the stored row returns it and writes no patient_changes row, before the changed_since_read check.

problems.scenario: 5. Result comes back after the visit is done (14 days later)
problems.detail: (a) HbA1c due in 3 months: due_at = now + 90 d → holds excludes it → Done closes the visit done; on day 90 the lab collects against the request from its own read_queue due window, no visit needed; result → review_needed_at → to-review; change_request still signals queue:IM for a done visit — a harmless refetch. (b) Culture, 5-day turnaround: Done → pending (holds 1); sweep → away; result day 5 → to-review; V pending ∧ away ∧ holds 0, invisible; lapsed 14 d after the away step. Both as designed. The strain is the two 14-day constants racing each other: a test due in 13 days (due_at < now + 14 d → holds → pending) → away on night 1 → drawn day 13, resulted day 14, patient returns day 15 → the sweep has already written lapsed (14 d idle from the away step) → open_visit finds no open visit → inserts a fresh WAITING row whose requests[] is empty because the request entry's visit_id is the lapsed visit → the doctor is handed exactly the hunt the holds window was written to prevent. The window promises a hold the lapse clock cannot keep.
problems.fix: One sentence in rule 7: idle for a pending, away visit is measured from the latest of its own steps and the request_steps of the requests that hold it. A result, collection or cancel on a held request restarts the 14 days; an abandoned request with no steps still lets the visit lapse. No constant moves, no column.

problems.scenario: 6. Patient at IM, sent to Cardiology the same day (two visits or one?)
problems.detail: Two visits, and both are honest. Dr A writes a consult request (type request, service to Cardiology, visit_id = V1); Done → holds(V1) = 1 (in-house, not a prescription, due now) → V1 pending, present → PENDING at IM showing 'consult at Cardiology · sent'. At the cardiology desk the correct call is open_visit(uuid, patient, Cardiology, 'routine', NULL, request_id): request open ∧ to_department_id = Cardiology ∧ requests.patient_id = patient (the survivor; open_visit already refused merged-away) → V2 waiting, present, is_first computed for Cardiology; visits_open is per department so V1 and V2 coexist. Cardiologist: waiting → in_consult; consult screen pre-fills reply_to_id := V2.request_id; final reply entry (visit_id = V2) → change_request → done → signal queue:IM (the request entry's visit is V1). IM refetch: V1 pending ∧ holds 0 ∧ seen → BACK with 'consult · Cardiology · done'. Cardiologist Done → holds(V2) = 0 (the request entry carries V1) → done. The strain: the desk has no way to learn request_id. read_patients hits carry open_visits[] but no open requests; the consult sits only in Cardiology's read_queue, another screen. A desk that clicks the plain Here opens V2 with request_id NULL: the consult screen pre-fills nothing, the cardiologist may write a note that is not a reply, the request stays open, V1 never turns BACK and Cardiology's queue prints 'consult not answered' against a done visit. Nothing is lost, but the two-click promise fails for the one visit type that exists to answer a request.
problems.fix: The read_patients hit (and read_patient) gains open_requests[] {request_id, service_name, to_department_id, requester_name} for open requests of type request addressed to a visited department the caller may read:queue; the Here on such a row passes request_id. A return-shape rule, no column; open_visit still infers nothing.

problems.scenario: 12. Three doctors, reception assigned nobody, Dr B opens the visit
problems.detail: V waiting, assignee_id NULL. Dr B: mark_visit(V, waiting, in_consult) → UPDATE … WHERE id = V AND status = 'waiting' → 1 row → seen_at, assignee := B, step. Dr C a second later: the UPDATE waits on B's row lock, re-evaluates the WHERE on the committed row → 0 rows → visit_moved with the current row (assignee B); C refetches. Correct: compare-and-set is the whole story. The strain is the other order: the desk assigned Dr A (assignee_id = A), A is late, Dr B takes the patient. 'assignee_id := caller when NULL' leaves A in the column, so the in_consult row prints 'with Dr A' while B is consulting, and after B sends her back to the queue the BACK row still says A. visit_steps has B as actor but nothing reads it for the queue.
problems.fix: One word in the moves table: assignee_id := caller on every in_consult, not only when NULL. Once a consult starts, who should see her and who is seeing her are the same person.

problems.scenario: 14. Lab-only walk-in with an outside paper request
problems.detail: Reception is is_visited, so open_visit(uuid, patient, Reception, …) succeeds (write:visit in the desk's own department) → V_r waiting, present, in read_visit_queue(Reception). The paper must become a record request before the lab can work it; the receptionist gains no record action, so a nurse or doctor with write:request writes it and must pick visit_id = V_r from a screen that is not a consult screen — a convention the draft leaves to spec 01. Then holds(V_r) = 1 until the lab replies. Now rule 11's promise 'BACK at the desk when the lab closes the request': rule 3 and section (e) define BACK = seen ∧ …, and seen_at is set only by in_consult, which 'never' happens here. The row stays WAITING (waiting ∧ unseen) from arrival to close; the change_request signal refetches it and requests[] flips to 'CBC · done', which is enough for the desk, but no band ever changes. The sweep then applies rule 1: waiting ∧ unseen ∧ idle 12 h → left, so a culture walk-in is 'left' on night one and the patient returning for the result gets a fresh visit with an empty requests[]. It works by convention; the text promises a band the query cannot produce.
problems.fix: Rewrite rule 11 in one line: a lab-only walk-in stays WAITING at the reception; its row's requests[] says when the result is in; the desk ends it waiting → done, or the sweep ends it left. Drop 'BACK at the desk'; nothing else moves.

problems.scenario: 15. Duplicate registration found after the visit started (merge later — what the visit layer must allow now)
problems.detail: B registered as a duplicate of A; V on B is in consult; entries land in B's record. The visit layer already allows what the later merge needs: visits.patient_id stays literal (the composite key entries (patient_id, visit_id) forbids rewriting it), is_first and read_patient read patient_id = ANY(ids), open_visit and register_patient will refuse B with patient_merged + survivor id, merge_patients refuses visit_open while B's visit is open, and requests.patient_id is re-keyed to A on merge (spec 01) while holds joins by entries.visit_id only, so holds survive. Two strains. (1) The draft contradicts itself on who may end B's visit: the moves table allows pending → cancelled with write:visit and a reason; the actions paragraph says reception 'may not touch … pending'. Under the prose a pending B visit (results out) blocks the merge for up to 14 days while B's record accumulates results the doctor reads under the wrong card. (2) visit_open carries no visit id, so the screen cannot offer 'cancel it and merge'.
problems.fix: Rule: the table wins — the desk may cancel a pending visit with a reason (it is 'its own mistake' by definition); the prose becomes 'may not move a visit into or out of in_consult, nor close pending as done'; merge_patients' visit_open refusal returns the open visit ids.

problems.scenario: 16. Deceased patient
problems.detail: There is no fact for it. A patient who dies with a pending, away visit: results arrive → to-review (safe); the visit lapses 14 d after away; nothing else happens, correctly. A patient known to have died: the record holds it as a problem or note, but read_patients 'is not a record read' and returns only the row, identifiers and open visits — so the desk sees a live namesake, can register a duplicate against a dead patient's warning row, or click Here and open a visit, and the queue prints him WAITING. open_visit cannot refuse what no column holds; the draft defers died_on explicitly and lists no known limit for the gap.
problems.fix: Ship the one nullable column now: patients.died_on (partial date) set by register_patient; open_visit refuses patient_died; the search hit carries it. Additive, nothing else reads it, and it is the only fact the desk must know before the record is opened. If the owner keeps it deferred, add 'no deceased marker at the desk' to known limits — a rule cannot do more because search is not a record read.

problems.scenario: 20. Returns within 14 days with a new complaint while a pending visit is open
problems.detail: Day 1 pending (culture out); away by sweep; day 3 result → to-review, phone call. Day 10 he is back with knee pain. read_patients → open_visits[] {V, IM, pending, away} → Here → open_visit returns V and marks present → BACK (pending ∧ holds 0 ∧ seen). The queue reads 'back, results in'; arrived_at and is_first are day 1's; the doctor opens V and sees the culture and the knee in one visit; Done closes it. Clinically fine, and a visit spans days by decision, but 'a visit row is an arrival' — a meaning that never changes — is false for this arrival, and the desk cannot start a fresh one: visits_open forbids a second open IM visit and pending → done needs mark:in_consult, so no desk action produces a new row without a doctor.
problems.fix: A known-limits line, not a move: 'a return within 14 days joins the open visit, whatever the reason; the queue prints arrived_at so the doctor sees the visit is 10 days old'. If the owner insists on a fresh row, the smallest widening is pending → done on write:visit — not recommended, because the desk would then be closing visits whose results are out.

problems.scenario: 21. Fasting bloods next morning, straight to the lab
problems.detail: Day 1: request due tomorrow 08:00 → holds (due < now + 14 d) → pending, present; away by desk or sweep. Day 2 07:45 the patient goes to the lab; the request is in read_queue(Laboratory) by due_at; the technician collects (pack step, request still open). 'The phlebotomist asks and clicks Here': staying → mark_present(V, true) — the technician's write:visit in Laboratory passes on IM through served_departments (laboratory, NULL) → V pending, present → PENDING at IM; result 09:30 → change_request → signal queue:IM → BACK. Going home → no click; result → to-review; the 14:00 return is scenario 4. The strain is the visit_id the technician's click needs: read_queue rows are requests, and spec 01 nowhere says the row carries the request entry's entries.visit_id; without it the lab screen must call read_patients (technician holds read:patient) and pick from open_visits[] — three clicks at the bench for the one visit call spec 03 asks a non-desk role to make. A second, smaller strain: a patient who says 'staying' and leaves after the draw sits in IM's PENDING then BACK until the sweep 12 h later, so 6 pm 'still here' lists him; only the phlebotomist's question protects it.
problems.fix: One additive field: read_queue rows carry the request entry's visit_id (an entries column already joined for display; 'public signatures only grow' allows it and (g) already amends 01). The 6 pm noise stays a convention.

problems.scenario: 23. Nurse-led clinic (a nurse practitioner consults)
problems.detail: The draft rejects doctor_id because a role name in a column is 'false in a nurse-led clinic', then gives mark:in_consult to the built-in doctor role alone, and spec 02 defers custom roles and the role editor. In a wound or diabetes-nurse clinic the nurse can open, Here and write entries but never move a visit: mark_visit(V, waiting, in_consult) is refused by the gate, so seen_at is never set, is_first is true on every visit, BACK is impossible (seen required), and sweep rule 1 marks every unseen visit left at 12 h idle after a full consultation. The owner's clinic is unaffected; the 'multi-department hospital, unchanged' promise is not.
problems.fix: One role_actions row: the built-in nurse role holds mark:in_consult. The gate says who may move; the screen says who does — an IM nurse's today's-fields screen simply has no consult button, so scenario 8 is unchanged.

problems.scenario: 24. Follow-up request written from the to-review screen
problems.detail: Dr A reviews the CBC at night in read_to_review and orders ferritin from that screen (write_request). The client sets entries.visit_id 'at write time (the consult screen's visit)' — this is not a consult screen and the to-review row does not say which visit its entry carries, so the ferritin entry gets visit_id NULL. holds(V) ignores it (joins on e.visit_id = V). Next day Here → BACK (holds 0) while ferritin is out; the row's requests[] lists only the CBC; the doctor calls him in with nothing new and sends him out again. Not a loss, and the entry is correct by spec 01; only the visit link is missing — exactly the hunt the derivation promises to end.
problems.fix: The same field as scenario 21 on read_to_review, plus one rule line in f.1: a request written from a request's screen carries that request's visit_id. No inference in write_entry, no column.

problems.scenario: Nurse and doctor update the same visit concurrently: mark_visit(V, waiting → in_consult) by the doctor, mark_present(V, false) and mark_visit_routing(V, priority = urgent) by the nurse, plus a second doctor's mark_visit(V, waiting → in_consult)
problems.detail: The status compare-and-set is sound if written as UPDATE visits SET status = 'in_consult', seen_at = coalesce(seen_at, now()), assignee_id = coalesce(assignee_id, caller) WHERE id = V AND status = 'waiting' RETURNING *: the second doctor's UPDATE waits on the row lock, re-evaluates WHERE under READ COMMITTED, gets 0 rows and raises visit_moved with the current row and the first doctor's name. The nurse's presence and routing UPDATEs carry no from_status, wait on the same row lock and apply on top (present_at NULL on an in_consult row is legal by rule 6; the consult row merely drops out of the queue read, since it filters present_at IS NOT NULL). The gap is visit_steps: pk (visit_id, position), position = max(position)+1. If change_visit computes the position BEFORE its UPDATE takes the row lock, two concurrent steps both read max = 1 and one fails on the pk (a raise the doctor sees as a random error, and the step history is what the CI refold checks). Nothing in the draft fixes the order; 'compare-and-set is the whole concurrency story' does not say the row lock orders the steps.
problems.fix: One sentence in (d) under change_visit: 'change_visit updates the visits row first (its row lock orders the steps), then inserts the step at max(position) + 1; a 0-row update raises visit_moved or visit_ended.'

problems.scenario: visit_steps after ten years (hospital scale) and the promised CI refold
problems.detail: Volume holds: 500 visits × ~6 steps × 365 × 10 ≈ 11 M rows, ~1 GB, pk (visit_id, position) only, UUIDv7 visit ids so the btree appends; reads are by visit_id (queue history, sweep's max(recorded_at) over a handful of rows per open visit), erase reaches steps through visits_history (patient_id, arrived_at DESC) then the pk. The strain is determinism of the fold that CI compares: arrived_at and the initial present_at must be read as row 1's recorded_at (row 1's changes carries no present_at), seen_at as the first in_consult step's recorded_at, ended_at as the terminal step's recorded_at — all derivable — but assignee_id is not: the first in_consult step sets assignee_id := caller when NULL and the draft gives that step no changes, while routing rows carry {assignee_id}. A refold must guess assignee from actor_id of the first in_consult step, which is exactly the 'step table that can contradict itself' (i) rejected.
problems.fix: One sentence in (b) visit_steps: 'the in_consult step carries {assignee_id} when it sets it; row 1's recorded_at is arrived_at and the first present_at.'

problems.scenario: read_patients at 100 000 patients with a transliteration typo (Muhammad for Mohammed), plus the all-digits path
problems.detail: pg_trgm pads each word with two leading and one trailing space: 'muhammad' → 9 trigrams, 'mohammed' → 9, shared 3 ('  m','ham','amm'), similarity 3/15 = 0.20 — below the 0.3 threshold, so the % operator and the GIN index return nothing for the family name alone; 'mohamed' vs 'mohammed' is 0.70 and fine. The duplicate warning is 'family name and birth year' → the daily Mohammed/Muhammad duplicate the spec names is exactly the one trigram misses (a full 'muhammad ali' vs 'mohammed ali' scrapes 0.37 only because ' ali' is shared). Two index details: a GIN over (organization_id, plain_name(…)) needs btree_gin for the uuid column — index the expression alone and filter organization_id after; and the btree (organization_id, digits(phone_text)) cannot serve the stated suffix match (LIKE '%' || q), so phone search is a 100 k-row scan (~10 ms, tolerable but the index is dead weight). Ranking otherwise holds: exact plain_name equality first, then similarity DESC LIMIT 20 over the % candidates, born_on year and phone digits as narrowing filters.
problems.fix: Rule + one index, no column: the duplicate warning compares dmetaphone(plain_name(family_name)) (fuzzystrmatch; MHMT for both spellings) with the birth year, alongside identifier and phone digits; index the phone as reverse(digits(phone_text)) text_pattern_ops and search LIKE reverse(q) || '%'.

problems.scenario: A department is retired with 12 patients waiting in it (open visits, no open requests)
problems.detail: Spec 02's retire_department refuses only department_has_open_requests / department_has_unreviewed_results, so the retire succeeds, and it deletes the department's user_roles and served_departments rows. From that commit: read_visit_queue(department) needs read:queue in that department → only everywhere-holders (the owner) pass; the clinic's doctors and its reception lose the 12 rows; read_patients shows open_visits[] only for departments the caller may read:queue, so a search does not reveal the stuck visit either; open_visit refuses department_retired for new arrivals. The 12 patients are physically waiting and invisible on every working screen. The desk re-opens each in the successor department (visits_open is per department, so allowed), is_first is freshly true for all twelve, and the old visits are swept to left/lapsed hours later. Nobody is lost clinically, but it is the hunt the owner forbade, for twelve people at once.
problems.fix: One line in (g)'s amendment to 02: retire_department also refuses department_has_open_visits (EXISTS visits WHERE department_id = id AND ended_at IS NULL).

problems.scenario: A doctor is retired (save_user, retired_at = now) while 12 waiting visits carry assignee_id = him
problems.detail: The composite key (organization_id, assignee_id) → users still holds (users are never deleted). The gate refuses his next call; the 12 rows stay in the queue showing his assignee_name. The draft's assignee sentence — 'NULL = anyone holding mark:in_consult here' — reads as if non-NULL restricts who may take the patient; if a builder enforces that, every one of the 12 is stuck until reception reroutes each by mark_visit_routing. If assignee is a hint (spec 01's requests.assignee_id reading), another doctor's mark_visit(waiting → in_consult) succeeds but 'assignee_id := caller when NULL' leaves the retiree on the row for the rest of the visit, and save_user's {open_assigned, to_review} return counts requests only, so the administrator is never told 12 visits pointed at him.
problems.fix: Two sentences: 'assignee_id is routing, never a gate; mark_visit checks it nowhere' and 'in_consult sets assignee_id := caller when NULL or when the assignee is retired'. (Optionally (g): save_user's open_assigned counts open visits too.)

problems.scenario: A result closes the last request; the clinic screen receives {entry_id} on queue:<clinic>
problems.detail: Section (e) fixes the client rule: 'refetches read_visit_queue on {visit_id} and read_queue on {entry_id}'. change_request's signal to the visit's department carries spec 01's payload {entry_id} (and (e) forbids any other payload). So when the lab's final reply folds the request to done, the clinic screen refetches only read_queue (its request queue) and does not refetch read_visit_queue — the band that just changed from PENDING to BACK. The database is right (the derivation is correct on the next read) but the doctor's screen shows the patient as PENDING until some other visit event on that department happens to fire a {visit_id}; in a quiet afternoon that is the doctor hunting for who came back from the lab, i.e. the one outcome the whole derivation was chosen to prevent. The same gap hides the BACK flip in the mark_present-vs-change_request scenario.
problems.fix: Rule, no schema: 'any signal on queue:<department> refetches both read_queue and read_visit_queue; the id in the payload is a hint, not a router' (both reads cost 1–3 ms and are debounced).

problems.scenario: open_visit finds the patient's open visit away and marks it present while the doctor's mark_visit(pending → done) commits in between
problems.detail: open_visit branches on a SELECT that sees V open and away, then calls change_visit to set present_at. If the terminal done commits first, the presence UPDATE … WHERE id = V AND ended_at IS NULL re-evaluates to 0 rows. With change_visit raising visit_ended on 0 rows (as mark_present's refusal implies) the desk sees an error and clicks Here again, which now inserts a new visit — one wasted click, no loss. If a builder instead 'returns the row' on 0 rows, the desk believes the patient is checked in while he is in no queue, and nobody notices until he complains: the draft's 'other parameters ignored, return it' wording invites that reading.
problems.fix: One sentence under open_visit: 'the presence step is compare-and-set on ended_at IS NULL; on 0 rows open_visit inserts a new visit instead of returning the old one.'

problems.scenario: A receptionist cancels a pending visit (results out) by mistake, and the rules in (c) and (d) disagree about whether she may
problems.detail: The moves table row 'waiting · in_consult · pending → cancelled | write:visit (out of in_consult: mark:in_consult)' lets a receptionist cancel a pending visit, while (d) says reception 'may not touch in_consult or pending' and the neighbouring row 'pending → done' needs mark:in_consult. Under the table's reading: the cancel ends the visit ('counts for nothing'), its requests stay open, the results reach to-review, and when the patient returns the desk's Here inserts a NEW visit whose holds are 0 (the requests' entries point at the cancelled visit) — he lands in WAITING as an unseen arrival, is_first false, and the doctor does not see him as BACK. Not a loss, but a rule contradiction that lands the returning patient in the wrong band.
problems.fix: Edit the table cell to 'write:visit (out of in_consult or pending: mark:in_consult)'.

problems.scenario: sweep_visits() listed as a public function with no gate, callable through the API
problems.detail: Spec 02's B9 grants authenticated EXECUTE on every function in schema public and requires every public function to start with require_access. The draft lists sweep_visits() among the public functions with 'no gate', so any logged-in user of any organization can call it for every organization at will. The effect is bounded (it only performs moves the next cron tick would perform within the hour, with actor_id NULL), and B16's tenant matrix skips it because it has no id parameter, but it is a door by spec 02's own definition and it would have to appear in B17's golden signatures as a public function that is not one. The runner precedent is core.run_pack_calls, named in B11's cron.job list — exactly where (g) already puts the sweep.
problems.fix: Name it core.sweep_visits() (private schema, pg_cron only), remove it from the public list, keep it in B11's cron.job list.

problems.scenario: Consult by visit when the patient already has an open walk-in visit in the consulted department today
problems.detail: Patient saw clinic B at 09:00 (VB, pending, bloods out). Clinic A sends a consult request to B; the patient walks to B's desk; open_visit(id, patient, B, priority, NULL, request_id) hits 'an open visit for (patient, department) → mark present when away and return it, other parameters ignored'. request_id is silently dropped: VB.request_id stays NULL, the consult screen has nothing to pre-fill reply_to_id from, write_entry never infers it (spec 01), so doctor B's note closes nothing unless he picks 'this note answers the consult' by hand; the request stays open on B's request queue and clinic A's visit stays PENDING on it. Nothing is lost (the request is visible work), but the desk was told the Here needs no decision and the drop is invisible to it.
problems.fix: One sentence under open_visit: 'when the open visit's request_id is NULL and the call carries one, open_visit writes a routing step {request_id}; when both are set and differ it returns the visit unchanged and the client shows the second consult as open work.'

problems.scenario: register_patient retried after a dropped connection (same client-minted id), and two desks editing one patient
problems.detail: Two desks: the second save carries the patient_change_id the screen loaded, a newer patient_changes row exists → changed_since_read; correct. Retry of a NEW registration: the first call committed the row and change row C1; the retry 'upserts on the client-minted id (a second call edits)' with the seen id it loaded (NULL) → a newer row C1 exists → changed_since_read on a registration that succeeded. The desk sees an error, searches, finds the patient, carries on — a loss of the two-click promise on every flaky save, and different from spec 01's 'a retry with the same id returns the stored row and changes nothing'. The single parameter patient_change_id also conflates spec 02's seen_change_id (the CAS) with the id of the row the call writes; the draft's patient_changes.id is listed but never client-minted, so the server has no retry key for the change itself.
problems.fix: Mirror spec 02: register_patient(…, seen_change_id, change_id) where change_id is the client-minted patient_changes.id; 'a patient_changes row with this id exists → return the row, nothing changes' before the CAS on seen_change_id.

problems.scenario: record_number as a bigint identity when two organizations share one database, and the legacy setval
problems.detail: An identity column is one sequence per table, not per organization: in a shared database organization A's cards read 1, 3, 7, … and B's 2, 4, 5, 6 — unique (the UNIQUE (organization_id, record_number) is then redundant) but gapped, and (h)'s 'a legacy restart is one setval' moves every organization's next number at once, so a clinic importing 20 000 legacy cards jumps its neighbour to 20 001. Harmless under spec 01's 'scale out = database per organization' and for a hospital that is one organization, but the sentence 'unique per organization' reads as if numbers were minted per organization, which they are not, and a builder may reach for the max+1-under-lock path (i) rejected.
problems.fix: One sentence in (h): 'one sequence per database: an organization sharing a database gets gapped numbers; a legacy restart needs its own database.'

problems.scenario: Appointments and no-show against a booking
problems.detail: The pack model works with zero ALTERs: `appointments.bookings (id, organization_id, patient_id, department_id, booked_for_at, priority, request_id null, visit_id null)` in the pack schema, core ids with no key (spec 02). Arrival is the desk's Here = `open_visit`, which is idempotent on the open (patient, department) row, so an early arrival, a booked patient who also walked in, and a patient whose last-week visit is still `pending` all resolve to one visit row; the pack then stores the returned `visit_id` on the booking. A no-show is `bookings.visit_id IS NULL` past `booked_for_at`; it never has a visit row, so `visits`, the sweep and the bands never see it. Two lines of the draft contradict this: (h) lists "`no_show` as an enum value when appointments exist" — a status no row could ever carry, because a visit row is an arrival ((h) never-change meaning) and a no-show never arrived; and (f)8 promises the pack EXECUTE on `open_visit`, which widens spec 02's locked pack grant list (funnels + public `read_`/`mark_` only; CI grants/B9) and contradicts (f)8's own first clause "packs never see visits". Within-band order is `arrived_at`, not slot time; a booking screen that wants slot order re-sorts on the client from its own rows — acceptable, but unsaid.
problems.fix: Rule only. Strike `no_show` from (h)'s additive list: "a no-show is a booking that never became a visit; `visits.status` never learns the word." Strike the last clause of (f)8: no pack ever executes a visit function; the client calls `open_visit` as the desk user and passes the returned id to the pack's own `appointments_mark_arrived(booking_id, visit_id)`. Add to (c)12: "order inside a band is arrival; a booking pack's slot order is its screen's."

problems.scenario: Inpatient admission as a ward visit spanning days (beds, transfers, the sweep)
problems.detail: An admission fits the never-change meanings with no column: the ward visit is the arrival (`arrived_at` = admission, `ended_at` = discharge, `department_id` = the ward responsible, `present_at` set for the whole stay); (b) says `department_id` is "not where the patient is standing", so a bed is an admissions-spec table `bed_stays (visit_id, department_id, bed_name, from_at, to_at)` — rows. Ward entries carry the ward `visit_id` through the existing `(patient_id, visit_id)` key; `admitted` is one `ADD VALUE` on the status enum (spec 01's convention). What corrupts state the day `open_visit` stops refusing `ward`: (1) sweep rule 2 "seen ∧ open ∧ (present ∨ status ≠ pending) ∧ idle 12 h → pending, away" — doses and notes are entries, not visit steps, so every inpatient is "idle" after each quiet 12 h; the sweep clears `present_at` and writes a `pending` step on every bed, every night, and the ward board empties. The draft rejected "a ward exemption in the sweep" ((i)) only because wards are refused at open today. (2) A transfer between wards has no move: `mark_visit_routing` carries `assignee_id | priority | is_first`, never `department_id`; ending ward A `done` and opening ward B is "an arrival" but splits one stay across two visit ids with nothing linking them — the later `admission_id` column or a pack table.
problems.fix: Two rules now, no column: (a) `sweep_visits` joins `departments` and skips type `ward` — a WHERE that matches nothing today, costs nothing, and cannot be forgotten when admissions ship; (b) decide that a transfer is a routing step `{department_id: [old, new]}` on the same visit (`mark_visit_routing` gains a defaulted `department_id` when admissions ship — "signatures only grow"; `visits_open` re-checks the new pair; "`department_id` is the department responsible" survives because responsibility is what moved). Beds stay in the admissions spec's table keyed by `visit_id`.

problems.scenario: Telemedicine presence
problems.detail: Traced: `open_visit` (row 1, present) → `mark_visit(waiting → in_consult)` by the doctor → note entries with `visit_id` → `done`. Nothing requires a building: `mark_visit` has no presence precondition, `in_consult` never touches presence, and the queue is `WHERE present_at IS NOT NULL`. But the draft defines `present_at` as "here since; NULL = not in the building" and the one-sentence says "presence (in the building)": under those words the desk must assert a falsehood (`mark_present(true)` for someone at home) to get the patient into `read_visit_queue` at all — a non-present visit is invisible, so the doctor cannot find or start it. The patient cannot assert it himself (spec 02's gate passes kinds `staff | machine | pack | importer`; patients come through `patient_access`, never `user_roles`), so reception or the doctor clicks when the call connects — fine. The mode (video/phone) is a fact about the consult, i.e. a `data` key on the note entry (spec 01 rule 1), not a visit column; the queue cannot say "video" without a client-side join to a telemedicine pack's `calls (visit_id, …)` rows, and the presence step's free-text `reason` is not returned by the queue.
problems.fix: One sentence in (a) and rule 6, no column: "present = available to be seen now, asserted by staff — in the building, on the line, or at the door of a home visit."

problems.scenario: Patient-portal self check-in
problems.detail: The patient can never be the caller: spec 02's `require_access` accepts kinds `staff | machine | pack | importer`, and patient users come through `patient_access`, never `user_roles`. So self check-in is a kiosk or Edge Function acting as a `machine` user of the reception department. Traced what that user needs: `read:patient` (`read_patients` with the card's digits → `record_number` exact), `read:queue` on the served departments (without it `read_patients` returns an empty `open_visits[]` and the kiosk cannot tell an open `pending` visit from none), and `write:visit` on the served departments for `open_visit` / `mark_present`. Spec 02's locked sentence "a machine user holds `write:` actions in one department and writes only replies to requests sent there" forbids exactly this. Second gap: `open_visit(id, patient_id, department_id, priority, assignee_id, request_id)` takes `priority` and `department_id` from the caller — a patient-driven kiosk could open a `stat` visit at any served clinic and nothing server-side stops it. Nothing loses a patient: `open_visit` is idempotent and `visits_open` collapses a kiosk-and-desk race into one row.
problems.fix: Rule only. (g) amends spec 02's machine sentence: "…or, in a `reception` department, opens visits and marks presence." One line in (d): "when the caller is kind `machine`, `open_visit` writes `priority = routine`, `assignee_id = NULL`, `request_id = NULL`." QR/consent state is the portal pack's own table; no column on `visits` or `patients`.

problems.scenario: Waiting-room TV board
problems.detail: The board is a `read_visit_queue(department_id)` client on `queue:<department_id>`, refetching on `{visit_id}` — read and channel exist; a reception board calls once per served department and merges, as (d) says. Calling a patient without the rejected `queue_number` works because every row carries `record_number` (the number on the card in the patient's hand) and `assignee_name` for `in_consult` rows: "1042 → Dr Okafor"; clinics have doctors, not rooms, so there is nothing else to show. Two awkward things: (1) the same row carries `given_name`, `family_name`, `born_on`, `sex` and `requests[] {service_name, to_department_name}` — "culture at Laboratory" on a public wall is a clinical disclosure that only client discipline prevents, and every `read:queue` holder receives it; (2) the board's identity: a receptionist's login on a wall screen is a shared credential, and the honest identity — a `machine` user holding `read:queue` — is the same widening of spec 02's machine sentence as the kiosk.
problems.fix: Rule only: a board is a `machine` user holding `read:queue` in the department (the one-line widening from the kiosk scenario), and (e) gains "a board shows `record_number`, `band` and `assignee_name`, nothing else". `read_visit_queue` and its return shape are unchanged.

problems.scenario: ED triage acuity (where does it live?)
problems.detail: Acuity is a clinical judgment on vitals, so by the draft's own test ("dropping it changes no reading of the record") it cannot be a visit column: it is a `triage` entry — an emergency pack type with `data.acuity`, written in the same set as the vitals, with `visit_id` — and re-triage is a newer entry. The visit's `priority` is its operational shadow: the nurse's client writes the set, then `mark_visit_routing(visit_id, NULL, 'stat', NULL)` (`write:visit`, nurse holds it); the `{priority}` routing step is the re-triage trail on the operational side. Two writes, not atomic — acceptable because the record never depends on the visit and a lost second write leaves a routine row the nurse sees and fixes. What three values cannot do: ESI and Manchester have five levels; `request_priority` is spec 01's enum with three, and ORDER BY `priority, arrived_at` cannot put ESI 4 before ESI 5. Door-to-doctor (`seen_at − arrived_at`), LWBS (`left`) and time-to-triage (the entry's `occurred_at`) all exist already.
problems.fix: Rule in (c): "acuity is a triage entry in the record; `priority` is its three-level shadow set by routing; a finer order is the emergency pack's screen over its own `triage` list joined to `read_visit_queue` on the client." No enum growth, no column.

problems.scenario: Group visits
problems.detail: Spec 01 already makes a group session one set per patient; here it is n visit rows at the department (n idempotent `open_visit` calls at the desk), n sets with each `visit_id`. Closing: `mark_visit(waiting → done)` per row under `write:visit` — n clicks, no batch, and `seen_at` never set because a nurse cannot enter `in_consult` (`mark:in_consult` is `doctor` only in the built-in roles; custom roles are later, spec 02). Consequences: `is_first` stays true for these patients in that department for ever, BACK can never appear for them (BACK needs seen), and a class the nurse forgets to close is swept `left` after 12 h (waiting ∧ unseen) — a false history for eight people who attended. Nothing is lost or mis-keyed; the awkwardness is nurse-led care leaving no `seen_at`, which the draft half-admits when it rejects `doctor_id` as "false in a nurse-led clinic".
problems.fix: Rows, no column: the built-in `nurse` role holds `mark:in_consult` (the owner's sentence "only a user holding the consult action" already makes the action, not the title, the gate), so a nurse-led session is n `in_consult → done` moves; the client's Done loops `mark_visit` over the selected rows. No group id.

problems.scenario: A home visit
problems.detail: Traced as a clinic visit whose doctor is the desk: the phone mints the id, `open_visit(id, patient, clinic, routine)` (doctor holds `write:visit`) → row 1 present → `mark_visit(waiting → in_consult)` → entries with `visit_id` → `done`. Offline-safe: client-minted ids, and a second `open_visit` returns the stored row. A forgotten one is swept to `pending, away` at 12 h and `lapsed` at 14 d; nothing is lost. Awkward only under the current words: rule 6's "presence is set by `open_visit`" puts a patient in his own kitchen "in the building", and for the seconds between open and `in_consult` the clinic board lists him as WAITING for the desk to call. Where the consult happened is a fact about the consult — the note entry's `data` or a `home_visit` type — never a visit column; `site_name` is a department label and a home is not a site.
problems.fix: The same one sentence as telemedicine ("present = available to be seen now, asserted by staff"); no column.

problems.scenario: Export of one patient's visits with the record (spec 01's closed-record rule)
problems.detail: Spec 01's appendix makes export, erase, split and research extract "one operation: everything where `patient_id` is in the record", and its key `entries (patient_id, visit_id) → visits` means an export without `visits` cannot be re-imported (the key fails on insert) and a research extract without `visit_steps` cannot compute waits. Rule 10 of the draft gives erase's table list; export has none. Traced what an export must carry: `patients`, `patient_identifiers`, `patient_changes`, `visits`, `visit_steps` by `patient_id = ANY(ids)`, inserted on import in reverse erase order, with `visits.request_id`'s deferrable key covering the entries → visits → requests → entries circle. Second gap: entries are self-contained (names copied into `data`) but visits are not — `department_id`, `assignee_id`, `visit_steps.actor_id`, `patient_changes.user_id` are bare ids under composite tenant keys, so an import into another organization (spec 01's split = export + import) cannot insert them unmapped, and who/where is lost unless the exporter joins settings at export time.
problems.fix: Rule in (c)10: "erase's list is export's list, in reverse order, over the same ids; the exporter writes names beside `department_id`, `assignee_id`, `actor_id` and `user_id`; an import into another organization maps departments by name and sets assignee, actor and user to the importer." Fixed now so `visits` never needs a name column later.

problems.scenario: A second MRN scheme after a merger of two organizations
problems.detail: Spec 01 forbids moving a patient between organizations, so absorbing organization B is export + import into A. Traced: each imported patient gets a fresh A `record_number` (identity, never taken) and its B number lands in `patient_identifiers (system = 'record_number:B', value)` — the rule already in (b). A desk typing B's old 1042 gets A's record 1042 as the exact hit and B's as an identifier hit; the desk picks; nothing is lost. Two strains: (1) `read_patients`' order — "all digits → record_number, then phone digits, then an identifier value; otherwise trigram over names" — never tries identifiers for a query with a letter, so `B-1042`, a passport `AB123456` or a national id with a check letter falls to name similarity and misses; the draft's strongest duplicate key is unsearchable. (2) `record_number` as a bigint identity is one sequence for every organization in the database: numbers interleave across tenants, and "a legacy restart is one `setval`" moves every organization's next number; turning identity into a per-organization sequence later is an ALTER on `patients`.
problems.fix: Rule (a): an identifier value is tried, trimmed and exact, for every query before the name search. Decide now (b): `record_number bigint NOT NULL`, minted by `register_patient` from a per-organization sequence that `create_organization` creates (`setval` per organization; still never typed, never reused). Neither touches the table later.

problems.scenario: GDPR erase (does erase_patient erase visits?)
problems.detail: Yes, it is in the rule: (c)10 has `erase_patient` deleting `patient_changes`, `visit_steps`, `visits`, `patient_identifiers`, `patients` after the record tables, and `visits.request_id`'s key is deferrable so the entries → visits → requests → entries circle clears in one transaction. Traced the rest: pack tables hold `visit_id` with no key (spec 02), so nothing blocks; `drafts.visit_id` (spec 01) must go before `visits` — spec 01's erase already deletes drafts, but the order should say so; an open, present visit vanishes from the queue on the next refetch (erase sends no signal — acceptable). The gap: rule 10 says "by `patient_id`" while every read and rule 9 use `patient_id = ANY(ids)`; erasing survivor S with M merged into it leaves M's visits, identifiers and `merged_into_id` pointing at a deleted S — the key fails and the erase aborts, or dangles — unless erase covers both, which spec 01 requires ("everything about one patient, including patients merged into them"). Residual: the merge's `patient_changes` row on the other patient carries S's id in `changes` — an id, not personal data.
problems.fix: One sentence in (c)10: "`erase_patient` deletes the spec 03 tables for the survivor and every patient merged into it, drafts first, then writes the `erasures` row." No column.

problems.scenario: Retiring a department that still has open visits (extra)
problems.detail: Spec 02's `retire_department` refuses on open requests and unreviewed results and then deletes the department's `user_roles` and `served_departments` rows. Open visits are not on its list: a clinic retired at 17:00 with three `pending` patients (bloods out, due tomorrow) leaves visits nobody can read (`read:queue` needs a role there or in a serving department, both deleted), `open_visit` refuses `department_retired` tomorrow, and the desk's Here silently opens a new visit at the successor clinic while the old ones lapse in 14 d with the results on the requester's to-review list. No patient is lost, but three visits are stranded and their BACK never shows anywhere.
problems.fix: One line in (g) amending spec 02: `retire_department` also refuses `department_has_open_visits` while `EXISTS (visits WHERE department_id = id AND ended_at IS NULL)` — the desk ends them first. No column.

killed: front-desk-flow: queue_number for the waiting-room screen and for calling the next patient — A column, a row lock on departments in two functions, a per-day re-minting rule tied to site time, a second read function, and a TV logged in as a receptionist — for a waiting-room screen nobody asked for. The number would not even be the calling sequence: the bands put BACK and urgent ahead of it, so '23 → Dr Ahmed' only works for in_consult rows, which the desk already sees by name the moment the doctor's Start signals queue:<department>. Clinics have doctors, not rooms; the receptionist points the patient at the door. Families adjacent in the queue already follow from open_visit called for each child in turn, sorted by arrived_at. If a waiting-room screen is wanted later, queue_number is one additive column minted in open_visit; nothing in spec 03 blocks it.

patient-identity: An unknown or unconscious patient is an ordinary row with a real number: `patients.is_identified` — The column's only consumers are a queue-card badge and an exclusion in the duplicate check. An internal-medicine outpatient clinic registers no unnamed patients for years, and the hospital case is an emergency department, which is not a core department type (clinic · reception · ward · ancillary · outside) — value is speculative for the first two years by the owner's own scaling path. The part of the idea that matters needs no schema and is one sentence spec 03 can state to close spec 01's deferred item: an unknown patient is an ordinary row with a real `record_number` and placeholder names the organization chooses; identification is `save_patient` writing the real names (audited) or `merge_patients` into an existing patient; never a temporary number. Without the flag the placeholder name is the badge, and a duplicate warning on two 'Unknown' rows is a warning, never a block. `is_identified` is a nullable-boolean-later if an emergency pack ever needs it; it goes on idea 9's additive list.

patient-identity: `patients.language_name` for the interpreter badge, nothing more — Speculative for the first two years by the proposer's own admission ('the one column the owner may drop today with no cost tomorrow'). Its only consumer is a badge on a queue card; a nullable `*_name` column is one migration later with no change in meaning, and nothing in v1 reads it. The owner's bar is absolutely simple, and the last two panels killed too little. It goes on idea 9's additive list as `language_name`.

naming: Keep in_consult and seen_at; define 'consult'; the consult action is mark:consult — Not an idea: it keeps the draft as drafted. Its only two surviving lines already live elsewhere — `mark:consult` (and the reason not to borrow `mark:started`/`mark:done`) is in the action-keys idea, and the one-line definition of 'consult' versus 'consult request' belongs in the words table. Kept as a separate item it pads a spec that must be shorter than 02.

ten-year-evolution: department_id is the department responsible, mutable through mark_visit routing; resources point at visits — Its one true sentence — `department_id` is responsibility, not location — already lives in the closed-meanings idea, and the `routing` step with `{department_id}` already lives in `visit_steps`; nothing here is needed to make a ward transfer work. Everything else designs tables spec 03 does not build and the clinic will not have for years (`beds`, `sessions`, `session_visits`, `telemedicine.calls`, theatre as an ancillary department); spec 03 must be shorter than 02, and shaping other specs' tables is exactly the kind of text that gets a locked spec reopened.

ten-year-evolution: priority reuses spec 01's priority type; acuity is a record entry — The premise is false: spec 01's appendix already names its type `request_priority`, so a `visit_priority (routine | urgent)` — the values the owner fixed — is the symmetrical name, not a second enum for one word. `stat` on a visit means nothing in a clinic queue for two years and is one `ADD VALUE` in its own file (spec 01's own enum rule) the day an emergency department exists. The acuity half restates spec 01 rule 5 and then designs a triage pack's after-write; both belong elsewhere. The draft stands: `visits.priority visit_priority (routine | urgent)`, every queue sorted `priority, arrived_at`.

ten-year-evolution: is_present means reachable for care now; portal, kiosk, geofence and boards are users rows — It reopens a spec 02 security decision (S13: a machine user holds `write:` only, in one department, no `read:` and no `mark:`) so that a kiosk and a waiting-room board that will not exist in two years can hold `mark:present` and `read:queue`; that is not a clarifying sentence, it is a new hole. Portal check-in is spec 02's `patient_access`, built later, and needs no text here. Widening the meaning of `is_present` from the owner's 'in the building' to 'on the line or at home' is speculation the clinic never needs, and a `tickets` table is a column argument for a board nobody asked for. `visit_steps.actor_id` already says who marked presence; nothing survives.
